# ebml

> A streaming, cursor-based EBML/Matroska library. An element is reported the
> moment its header arrives and the caller decides on that header whether the
> payload is worth reading, so a live stream is an ordinary input rather than a
> special case. Implementations live under `impl/`, one directory per language;
> `spec/SPEC.md` is the contract they share.

This file indexes the documents an assistant should read before answering about
this project or writing code against it. It states nothing itself: every fact
lives in exactly one of the files below, and duplicating one here is how the
copies drift apart.

## Before proposing or adding an API

- [Declined additions](docs/design-rules/declined-additions.md): why the small
  cross-section IS the product, the three questions every proposed addition
  faces, and the ledger of what has been asked for, refused and accepted. The
  room to add convenient API here is large and deliberately unused — read this
  before concluding that a missing helper is an oversight.
- [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md): every standing rule in one line each, with a link to
  the note that argues it. The rules are the summary; the notes are the reasons.

## The contract

- [spec/SPEC.md](spec/SPEC.md): the normative, language-neutral portable
  contract. Where a design note and this document disagree, this one wins.
- [Pull shape across languages](docs/pull-shape-across-languages.md): why a
  caller-fed cursor keeps an explicit `Next` while a source-owning driver is an
  iterator, worked through Go, Rust, Python, JavaScript, Java, C# and C. Read
  before porting the reading surface.

## Design notes (not normative)

- [Index of all notes](docs/README.md)
- [Layer boundaries](docs/design-rules/layer-boundaries.md): layout, module
  path, what is core, `ext` leaves, integrations, retention.
- [Pull shape and node lifetime](docs/design-rules/pull-and-lifetime.md): one
  reading surface, the enforced node lifetime, where an iterator is allowed.
- [Errors, recovery, and delivery](docs/design-rules/errors-and-recovery.md):
  the two error classes, per-class recovery, the salvaged truncated tail,
  in-band failures.
- [The writer, round-tripping, and CRC-32](docs/design-rules/writer-and-crc.md):
  one encoder, byte-identical round-trip, explicit CRC.
- [Registry, boundary policy, schemas](docs/design-rules/registry-and-schemas.md):
  where element knowledge lives, the deny-only boundary rule, the CC-BY schemas.
- [Evidence over assumption](docs/design-rules/evidence-over-assumption.md): why
  a fixture or example models the shape the field produces.

## Using the library

- [README.md](README.md): what the library is, the implementation table, the
  `ebml` command, and what every implementation shares. Language-neutral.
- [impl/go/README.md](impl/go/README.md): the WHOLE of the Go library
  documentation — package map, dependency direction, entry-point selection,
  usage, writing. Go usage has exactly one home and this is it.

## Amazon Kinesis Video Streams

- [impl/go/integrations/kvs](impl/go/integrations/kvs): a SEPARATE Go module
  (`github.com/yacchi/ebml/impl/go/integrations/kvs`). Requiring
  `github.com/yacchi/ebml/impl/go` does not make it resolvable — it needs its
  own `go get`. It supplies the typed per-fragment `Metadata`, `ParseTimestamp`,
  `MetadataComplete`, the wall-clock accessors for a `Cluster.Timestamp` that
  counts from the Unix epoch rather than from the start of the stream, and a
  `Reader.Next` that REPORTS the in-band failure GetMedia states as
  `AWS_KINESISVIDEO_ERROR_CODE`. A consumer who reimplements these by hand
  usually misses that last one, and then a stream stopped by a KMS-key error
  reads as a clean end of stream.
- [impl/go/integrations/kvs/examples/getmedia](impl/go/integrations/kvs/examples/getmedia):
  a runnable end-to-end consumer.
